draft.title: Concentration
card: Concentration tells you how much solute is dissolved in a given volume of solution. The solute is the substance that dissolves, and the solution is the solute and solvent mixed together.
Molar concentration
c = n ÷ V, where c is in mol/L, n is the moles of solute and V is the volume of solution in litres. Change mL to L by dividing by 1000.
Mass concentration
mass of solute ÷ volume of solution, usually in g/L. To change g/L to mol/L, divide by the molar mass of the solute.
Parts per million
ppm means mg of solute per kg of solution. For dilute water solutions, 1 ppm is about 1 mg/L.
draft.remember: Concentration is solute per volume of solution: mol/L uses moles, g/L uses mass.

a.q: Liam dissolves 0.50 mol of sodium chloride in water to make 250 mL of solution. What is the concentration?
a.why: 250 mL is 0.250 L, so c = 0.50 ÷ 0.250 = 2.0 mol/L. Using 250 in place of 0.250 gives 0.0020 mol/L, so the volume must be in litres first.
a.clue: Convert the volume to litres before you divide.

b.q: A sample of sodium hydroxide solution has a concentration of 4.0 g/L. The molar mass of NaOH is 40 g/mol. What is its concentration in mol/L?
b.why: Divide the mass concentration by the molar mass: 4.0 g/L ÷ 40 g/mol = 0.10 mol/L. Multiplying by the molar mass gives 160, which is tempting but turns grams into the wrong unit.
b.clue: Grams per litre become moles per litre when you divide by the molar mass.

problems.detail: The first bullet defines concentration as solute in a given volume of solution, but the card's own ppm definition is mg of solute per kg of solution, which is per mass, not per volume. Concentration is better defined as the amount of solute in a given quantity (volume or mass) of solution.
The remember line says concentration is always solute per volume of solution. This conflicts with the card's ppm definition (mg per kg of solution) and leaves ppm out.

proposal.title: Concentration
card: Concentration is the amount of solute in a given quantity of solution, measured by volume or by mass. The solute is the substance that dissolves, and the solution is the solute and solvent mixed together.
Molar concentration
c = n ÷ V, where c is in mol/L, n is the moles of solute and V is the volume of solution in litres. Change mL to L by dividing by 1000.

Parts per million
ppm means mg of solute per kg of solution. For dilute water solutions, 1 ppm is about 1 mg/L.
proposal.remember: Match the unit to the measure: mol/L uses moles, g/L uses grams and ppm uses mg per kg.

a.clue: Convert the volume to litres before you divide.

b.clue: Grams per litre become moles per litre when you divide by the molar mass.
